extracted.intended_audience: media officers, legal and communications staff of Participating Clubs in the FIFA Intercontinental Cup 2025
extracted.subtask_description: Official Media and Marketing Regulations that prescribe how Participating Clubs (their Team Delegations and affiliates) must manage media access, branding, digital content, trophies, recordings, and Club media activities during the FIFA Intercontinental Cup 2025. Covers permitted/prohibited uses, approvals, and operational obligations for training, matchday, hotel, transport and digital behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training session media access
rubrics_metrics.description: All Participating Club training sessions shall be open to the media for at least 15 minutes following their commencement (with the exception of one training session prior to each Competition Match which cannot be the official training session on the day prior to a Matchday). The Participating Club shall inform FIFA, in writing, if it intends to exclude media representatives and FIFA Officials from a training session after providing them with 15 minutes’ access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs may exclude media after the initial 15 minutes only if FIFA is informed in writing. Under no circumstances will FIFA Officials or media representatives be permitted to enter the pitch before, during or after such training session.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory availability of coach and players for official media activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating Clubs must make their head coach and at least one player available to media representatives before/after training sessions and attend Official FIFA/LOC Media Activities (press conferences/mixed zones) at the Competition Stadium associated with their match.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An official press conference and/or mixed zone organised by FIFA on the day preceding the Matchday must be attended by the head coach and at least one player likely to be in the starting XI. If no press conference is organised, the coach and at least three players should be available in the mixed-zone around the training pitch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Player attendance substitution for press duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Attendance of a player at the press conference may be replaced by making at least three players available for interviews in a mixed-zone area around the training pitch for the official training session.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides an alternative to single-player attendance at press conferences; similarly, if a press conference is not organised, three players should be made available in the mixed-zone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matchday dressing room and upon-arrival media access
rubrics_metrics.description: Sufficiently in advance of arrival, and in coordination with FIFA, host broadcaster and an official FIFA photographer shall be granted access to the Participating Club’s dressing room for filming and photos, including unilateral stand-up interviews by up to two Media Partners. Upon arrival of the Team Delegation, the head coach or other Team Delegation members shall be made available for 'upon arrival' interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access must be coordinated with FIFA and the host broadcaster. Dressing-room filming is limited to the access and conditions specified (including the number of Media Partners and approved activities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-match flash interviews and mixed-zone participation
rubrics_metrics.description: After each Competition Match, the head coach and certain players must give interviews as flash interviews on the pitch near the technical area and in the players’ tunnel or close to team dressing rooms. All players who took part must pass through the mixed zone after the final whistle and be available for interviews; mixed-zone activities should conclude no later than 60 minutes after the final whistle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The head coach must attend the official post-match press conference; players who receive individual awards (e.g., Player of the Match) must attend related activations (photos, trophy acceptance). Players selected for doping control must remain available for flash interviews prior to doping control, accompanied by an official chaperone and a FIFA Media Officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-match Player of the Match obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The player selected as 'Player of the Match' will be required to participate in related post-match activation, including appearing for a photograph in front of the Presenting Partner’s backdrop and accepting the commercially branded trophy associated with the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation in these activations is mandatory as part of post-match obligations and commercial partner commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Players to sign memorabilia on request
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Participating Club agrees to ensure that its players cooperate in the signing of memorabilia items, the nature and quantity of which will be communicated by FIFA in due course (e.g. armbands, official jerseys) that have been committed to Commercial Partners by FIFA/LOC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs must ensure player cooperation for signing items committed to Commercial Partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official media activities free of third‑party advertising/branding
rubrics_metrics.description: All Official FIFA/LOC Media Activities shall be free of all advertising or branding materials relating to any third party (including Club Affiliates or any third party contracted to the Participating Clubs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restriction includes backdrops, signage, products, services and branding on equipment or apparel other than as permitted by the Equipment Regulations or other specified articles (7.1 to 7.5 references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on club media guides/publications at Official Activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Media guides and other publications may not be distributed by or on behalf of any Participating Club, Club Affiliate and/or any other third party at any Official FIFA/LOC Media Activities, unless previously approved by FIFA in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior written FIFA approval is required to distribute club-produced publications at Official FIFA/LOC Media Activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verbal reference prohibitions by players and delegation members
rubrics_metrics.description: Players and other Team Delegation Members may not make any verbal reference to: a) any Club Affiliate and/or any third party contracted to the Participating Clubs; b) any sponsor of a Team Delegation Member; or c) any other commercial entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies during Official FIFA/LOC Media Activities and is intended to avoid unauthorised commercial promotion or association.

rubrics_metrics.name: No advertising or promotional materials at Team Hotels
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise specifically confirmed in writing by FIFA for certain non-centralised Competition Matches, Participating Clubs are not permitted to display, arrange for the display of, or authorise the distribution of any advertising or other promotional materials at Team Hotels, including in internal public areas or external grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: article 11.2 iii) (Club Media Activities at Team Hotels special room) and limited training-shirt sponsor recognition under article 10.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor recognition on training shirts at hotels
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding article 7.1, training shirts and supplementary Equipment items worn by Team Delegation Members at Team Hotels may display the branding of Club Affiliates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a narrow exception allowing club-affiliate branding on training apparel at Team Hotels; broader advertising/display prohibitions still apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: FIFA filming access at Team Hotels
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon reasonable request, FIFA, FIFA Content Production Crews or their nominees shall have a dedicated interview room within a Team Hotel for the purpose of conducting interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs must provide a dedicated interview room within the Team Hotel as reasonably requested by FIFA or its nominees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistance with hotel media activities subject to privacy/sporting concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Participating Club must assist, and must ensure that each Team Delegation Member assists, to a reasonable extent, FIFA in its media activities at Team Hotels, it being understood that sporting concerns and the privacy of Team Delegation Members shall prevail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs and players should cooperate with FIFA media activities at hotels, but legitimate sporting or privacy issues take precedence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controlled Areas: no promotional/distribution activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise specifically confirmed in writing by FIFA, Participating Clubs must not, and must ensure Team Delegation Members do not, use, display or distribute any materials, or conduct any activities, in the Controlled Areas which may be used to identify and/or promote any third party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: i) no distribution of media guides or publications inside Controlled Areas without FIFA approval; ii) no selling/distribution of food/beverage items within Controlled Areas; iii) no selling/distribution of merchandise; iv) no display of advertising/branding materials relating to Club Affiliates or other commercial entities, except as permitted by other articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press backdrops for Club Media Activities outside Controlled Areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Press backdrops used by a Participating Club during any Club Media Activity may feature advertising/branding relating to third parties (such as Club Affiliates) only if they: a) do not create any association with FIFA/the Competition (in FIFA’s opinion); b) do not display Competition Marks or reference to FIFA/the Competition; c) display the Participating Club emblem; and d) indicate the relationship between the third party and the Participating Club (e.g. 'Official Sponsor of the Participating Club').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any such press backdrop used outside Controlled Areas during the Competition Period requires prior written approval from FIFA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location restrictions for Club Media Activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Other than specified exceptions, no Club Media Activity may be held inside any Controlled Area. Permitted locations include: a special room at Team Hotels (not visible from lobby) and enclosed rooms at Official Training Sites designated by FIFA, provided all other provisions are complied with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Team Hotels special room must not be the hotel lobby nor visible from the lobby; prior FIFA compliance and approvals apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on personal recording devices in Controlled Areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise agreed with FIFA in writing under a Participating Club Footage Licence Agreement, Participating Clubs must ensure that Team Delegation Members do not use, license or consent to use moving images recorded by personal recording devices in the Controlled Areas (except for Team Hotels) for distribution, broadcast and/or transmission over any form of media. This prohibition extends to any recording devices used by or with the knowledge of Participating Clubs in Controlled Areas (except Team Hotels).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict prohibition on distributing personal-device footage recorded in Controlled Areas unless exception agreed in writing by FIFA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Club video recording for technical analysis — permission and strict conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating Clubs are permitted to make their own recordings of Competition Matches solely for technical performance analysis, subject to conditions and a Participating Club Footage Licence Agreement: one camera per club, camera identification sticker, filming only from FIFA-specified location, only light amateur equipment, bib distributed by FIFA must be worn, only accredited team members may record, filming only for technical analysis, prohibited in dressing rooms/mixed zone/press conferences, and no commercial exploitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional details: only one bib will be distributed and must be returned after last match; FIFA’s determination on equipment being 'light, amateur' is final; breaches may make FIFA liable to commercial partners and cause damage for which clubs may be held responsible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute prohibition on commercial exploitation of FIFA-controlled images
rubrics_metrics.description: Under no circumstances may any images taken within a FIFA-controlled environment be used for any type of commercial exploitation, either during or after the Competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies irrespective of who recorded the images and is reiterated as likely to put FIFA in breach of its commercial agreements if violated; clubs may be held responsible for damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition Stadium advertising control
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise confirmed in writing by FIFA, the only advertising permitted in Competition Stadiums is that of the Commercial Partners erected by FIFA. Participating Clubs are not entitled to display, arrange for the display of, or authorise the distribution of any advertising or other promotional material whatsoever in the Competition Stadiums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a comprehensive prohibition on club or third-party advertising in stadiums, subject only to written exceptions by FIFA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of technical equipment and beverage restrictions in stadiums
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrictions relating to technical equipment and beverages outlined elsewhere also apply in Competition Stadiums unless otherwise confirmed in writing by FIFA for certain non-centralised Matches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See referenced articles (e.g., 7.4 and 7.5) for specific technical equipment and beverage provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance and promotional restrictions at stadium training sessions
rubrics_metrics.description: All training sessions at Competition Stadiums are controlled by FIFA and the LOC; Participating Clubs, Club Affiliates and third parties may not run any promotion associated with attendance at a training session nor sell tickets for attendance at training sessions at Competition Stadiums unless confirmed in writing by FIFA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs cannot monetise or promote attendance at stadium training sessions; all such sessions are under FIFA/LOC control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Training Sites usage window and commercial restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: From three days prior to the Participating Club’s first Competition Match until the conclusion of its final Competition Match, Participating Clubs shall use only the Official Training Sites designated by FIFA. If a pre-Competition site is used as an Official Training Site, it must be free of any and all commercial activities and identification other than those of the Commercial Partners at least three days prior to the first Competition Match.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforces exclusive use of FIFA-designated training sites in the critical pre-Competition window and removal/absence of third-party commercial identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team transportation branding and exclusive bus provision
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Participating Club will be provided a dedicated team bus for Competition Period transport (except certain non-centralised Matches). This team bus shall be the only transportation used by players and officials for Competition-related events. Except for Commercial Partners and FIFA-approved slogans, no promotional materials of any third party (including Club Affiliates) may be displayed on or inside the bus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other vehicles taken into Controlled Areas must be free of branding except manufacturer branding, Commercial Partners and FIFA/Competition branding; clubs/Team Delegation Members may not remove such branding; no third-party promotional materials allowed on vehicles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Friendly matches conditions and no association with Competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating Clubs may organise friendly matches in a Competition Territory before the Competition Period provided FIFA is notified of times/locations, prior written consent of FIFA and the Host is obtained, matches are not played in Competition Stadiums, and no association with the Competition is created (no Competition Marks, no verbal association such as 'The Road to...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even with consent, promotional/marketing materials for friendlies must not create an association with the Competition or use Competition Marks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team Media Centre (TMC) establishment and cost responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A Participating Club may establish its own Team Media Centre before and during the Competition. All costs for installation and management of TMCs shall be borne solely by the Participating Club concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs are responsible for TMC costs and must ensure TMCs comply with applicable regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on participation in social functions and external promotions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Participating Club shall ensure Team Delegation Members are available for a minimum of one official luncheon and one official training session and shall ensure neither the club nor its delegation members engage in any social function, promotional activity or event other than those conducted/organised by the official sponsors of the Competition, except as otherwise stated or approved by FIFA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs must seek FIFA approval for any activity outside official sponsor events; the rule protects official sponsor rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Media posting restrictions inside Controlled Areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Team Delegation Members are strictly prohibited from uploading or posting any Competition-related content during their presence inside a Controlled Area during the Competition Period (except from Team Hotels).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content posted from Team Hotels must be confined solely to the poster’s own personal Competition-related experience and must not interview or post stories about other Team Delegation Members, opposition members, or FIFA Officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and content taste standards for digital posts
rubrics_metrics.description: Team Delegation Members shall not disclose confidential or private information compromising security, staging, organisation, or privacy. Any content uploaded or posted shall be in the spirit of fair play, dignified and in good taste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content may not compromise competition security or privacy of individuals; FIFA may judge breaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited use of Competition-related words on personal digital media
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as explicitly otherwise set forth, Team Delegation Members shall not use any Competition Marks. They may however use certain word marks (e.g., 'FIFA Intercontinental Cup™', 'Intercontinental Cup') on their Digital Media or blogs provided the word 'FIFA' and other related words are not associated with any third party or used for commercial purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of these word marks is restricted to non-commercial editorial/personal uses and must not create association with third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on commercial references and ambush marketing online
rubrics_metrics.description: Team Delegation Members are prohibited from including any commercial reference in connection with uploaded/posted content; no advertising/sponsorship opportunities may be offered/sold connected to FIFA- or Competition-related content, and they must refrain from using uploaded/posted content for Ambush Marketing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also prohibits entering into exclusive agreements with third parties for uploading/posting FIFA-related content; domain names including 'FIFA' or 'Intercontinental Cup' or permutations are not permitted to be established or used by any Team Delegation Member.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted third-party sharing of Competition content with no association
rubrics_metrics.description: Team Delegation Members may upload/post FIFA- or Competition-related content on third-party Digital Media provided, in FIFA’s opinion, no association is created between such third parties and the Competition and that such content is not used for commercial purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FIFA retains subjective control in determining whether an association is created.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to link to FIFA and personal liability for online commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: Team Delegation Members uploading/posting Competition-related content are encouraged to link their blogs to FIFA.com or other FIFA digital media. They are solely responsible for their commentary and may be held personally liable for defamatory, obscene or proprietary content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encouragement to link aids official information flow; clubs should remind members of legal liability risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trophy custody and non-association with Club Affiliates
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating Clubs may be provided and permitted to retain certain Winner’s Trophies but Club Affiliates or third parties contracted to any Participating Club may not create an association between themselves and any Original or Winner’s Trophies (including replicas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restrictions include not displaying Winners’ Trophies at Club Media Activities with non-Commercial Partner branding, not parading/displaying them at events featuring club-affiliate branding, and prohibiting Club Affiliates from using images of the trophies in publicity or promotional materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on unofficial replicas and limits on authorised miniature replicas
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for miniature replicas produced by FIFA’s manufacturer with prior written approval, Participating Clubs are not entitled to produce their own unofficial replicas. Miniature replicas may be produced (by FIFA’s manufacturer) only if they do not exceed 15cm, are 'to scale', and individuals undertaking not to use such replicas for any commercial purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to appoint FIFA’s manufacturer must be approved in writing; museums or displays require FIFA permission; miniature replicas remain subject to strict non-commercial undertakings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trophy portrayal and merchandise prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: No images of the Original Trophies or the Winner’s Trophies may be used or licensed for use on items of clothing or other merchandise; Original Trophies remain FIFA trademarks and Participating Clubs have no right or licence to use photographs of the trophies for any commercial purpose other than purely editorial purposes to accompany written text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs must remind photographers, press and media of these restrictions prior to trophy presentations; breaches risk trademark infringement and commercial conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trophy custodial responsibilities and return/approval conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Winner’s Trophies may remain in temporary custody of the Participating Clubs but remain FIFA property and must be returned immediately if requested. Trophies may not be provided to third parties for display/use without FIFA’s prior written permission; any tours featuring the Winner’s Trophies must be approved in advance in writing by FIFA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs must take all reasonable steps, at their expense, to ensure security of Winner’s Trophies while in their possession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions for past winners on trophy movement and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Trophies awarded to past Participating Clubs must remain within the club’s direct control and should not leave the club’s home country without prior written consent of FIFA. Clubs must ensure Winner’s Trophies are presented in the historical context of the competition and not used in any way that could lead to association by any third party with the Original Trophy, the Competition or previous editions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs and their affiliates may not be granted rights or visibility where the Trophy is present; prohibition also applies to parading or photo shoots with the trophies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merchandising restrictions for past winners
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating Clubs awarded a Winner’s Trophy in previous editions are prohibited from developing, creating, using, selling or distributing any promotional materials or merchandise bearing any representation of the Original Trophy or any mark referring to any past edition of the Competition. Neither an Original Trophy nor any stylised representation may be portrayed on any Digital Medium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absolute ban on merchandise and digital portrayals tied to past Competition trophies to protect FIFA’s commercial rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional trophies subject to same conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: At FIFA’s discretion, additional trophies may be awarded during the Competition, subject to the same conditions as set out for Winner’s Trophies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any additional trophies follow identical custody, use, replica, merchandising and approval restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted use of Competition Marks by Participating Clubs — editorial only
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon FIFA approval, the Competition Marks and the Composite Logo may only be used by Participating Clubs for the purpose of referring descriptively to their participation in the Competition; all commercial or promotional use by Participating Clubs, their Club Affiliates or any third party contracted to them is strictly prohibited. These provisions apply from the date the regulations come into force and continue after the Competition Period until FIFA notifies otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs must obtain FIFA approval to use marks even for descriptive editorial purposes; commercial exploitation is forbidden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition Name editorial-use requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating Clubs are required, whenever referring to the Competition, to only use the Competition Name and each use must be in an editorial context only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents clubs from using the Competition Name in promotional or commercial campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite Logo creation and approval process
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating Clubs are permitted to create a Composite Logo incorporating the Official Emblem(s) and the Participating Club’s own emblem with the descriptive designation 'Finalist'. No other mark may be included without FIFA’s written permission. The Composite Logo must be submitted to FIFA in writing for approval prior to use; materials to form a Composite Logo may be downloaded from FIFA’s digital archive upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All uses of the Composite Logo must also be submitted for FIFA approval; other marks must not be placed near the Composite Logo in a way that confuses inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proximity and prohibited uses of Competition Marks/Composite Logo
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither the Competition Marks nor the Composite Logo may be used in proximity to names, logos or trademarks of Club Affiliates or any third party other than the Commercial Partners. They may not be used as part of advertising/promotional activity or strapline in connection with any Club Affiliate; on gifts, premiums, merchandise for sale; or on official printed matter that also displays names/logos of Club Affiliates (except FIFA-appointed Commercial Partners).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protects the exclusivity of Competition Marks and prevents implicit endorsement of third parties; exceptions require FIFA approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Club-printed materials editorial context and approval requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Club printed or electronic materials produced in relation to their participation (posters, guides, media guides, programmes, magazines, maps, booklets, electronic publishing etc.) must not feature Competition Marks or the Composite Logo other than in a purely editorial context. If Competition Marks appear on front/back cover in editorial context, no commercial identifications or advertisements may appear on those covers. All such printed materials must be submitted for FIFA’s approval in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers/titles must clarify publication is of the Participating Club and not FIFA (e.g., 'Official [Name of Publication] for [Team] at the FIFA Intercontinental Cup 2025™'). Competition Marks may appear inside only in editorial context and not opposite pages displaying advertisements.

rubrics_metrics.name: No association with Club Affiliates in promotional materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating Clubs must ensure no association is created between their Club Affiliates (or third parties contracted to the Club) and the Competition in any of their promotional materials. Club Affiliates and third parties shall not use any of the Competition Marks or the Composite Logo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict prohibition to prevent club affiliates from leveraging Competition association; clubs must police affiliates' promotional activities.
